instructions: Cut the beef into 1 1/2-inch cubes and pat them dry. Toss them with 1 tsp of the salt, the pepper and the flour until they're lightly coated.

Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a large heavy pot over medium-high heat. Add half the beef in a single layer and leave it alone until the underside is golden brown, about 3 minutes. Turn the pieces and brown them for 3 minutes. Transfer to a plate and brown the second half the same way.
Meanwhile, finely chop the onion, mince the garlic, and cut the carrots into thirds. Peel the potatoes and cut them into 1 1/2-inch chunks.
Turn the heat to medium and add the remaining 1 tbsp oil to the same pot. Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes, stirring, until soft.
Add the garlic and the paprika. Stir for 30 seconds, until it smells fragrant.
Add the carrots and the wine and scrape up the browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Let it bubble for 2 minutes.

Return the beef and its juices to the pot. Add the tomatoes, broth, bay leaves and the remaining 1/2 tsp salt. Bring to a simmer, then partly cover, turn the heat to low, and cook for 1 hour, stirring now and then, until the beef is tender when you press it with a spoon. Add a splash of water if it gets dry.
Add the potatoes, stir them in, and cook for 20 minutes, until they're tender when a knife goes in.
Stir in the peas and cook for 2 minutes. Take out the bay leaves.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
method_notes: No version I could read showed a rating, so this is a fallback lead: the Directo al Paladar classic (312 votes, no average shown) browns floured beef, builds the sauce with onion, garlic, carrots, red wine and tomato, and adds the potatoes late. Spanish Fiestas adds paprika and white wine, and Camila Made uses a longer, thicker braise. I followed the lead and added the paprika and a longer potato time so the potatoes hold up. The page's own amounts for broth were small, so I used 1 cup.
